question.text: Priya purchased a life insurance policy on 15th June 2023 with a sum assured of Rs.10,00,000 and an annual premium of Rs.60,000. She received the maturity proceeds of Rs.12,50,000 in June 2033. Under Section 10(10D), what is the tax treatment of the maturity proceeds?

answer.text: Fully taxable as the premium exceeds 5% of the sum assured
Fully exempt because the policy completed ten years
Exempt up to Rs.10,00,000 and balance taxable
Fully exempt as the annual premium does not exceed 10% of the sum assured and does not breach the high-premium threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: For non-ULIP life insurance policies issued on or after 1 April 2012, the workbook gives a 10% sum-assured threshold: maturity proceeds are exempt under Section 10(10D) if the annual premium does not exceed 10% of the sum assured. For policies issued on or after 1 April 2023, an additional high-premium rule applies — exemption is denied when the annual premium (or aggregate premium across eligible policies) exceeds Rs.5,00,000. Priya's premium of Rs.60,000 is 6% of the Rs.10,00,000 sum assured (well within the 10% test) and is far below the Rs.5,00,000 high-premium threshold, so both source-backed tests are satisfied and the maturity proceeds are fully exempt. The Trap: Option A applies an unsupported 5% threshold; the workbook uses 10% for the sum-assured test, with the post-April-2023 rule keyed off a Rs.5,00,000 premium ceiling rather than a 5% ratio. Option B treats long policy duration as sufficient on its own, which it is not. Option C invents a partial-exemption ceiling. Note: The two source-backed conditions are (i) annual premium not exceeding 10% of sum assured (for policies on or after 1 April 2012), and (ii) for policies on or after 1 April 2023, the additional aggregate-premium ceiling of Rs.5,00,000.
